title: Over a field, few differentials at a point imply smoothness there
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\Omega_{S/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. If $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S),$$ then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].
